title: Allowed Environments
after: after Lab 5 (parameters); one resource group, no container group
space: the student's own Dojo Cloud subscription (`{user}`), its resource group `rg-{user}-c1` (the only assignment scope), and their own repo `{user}/challenge-c1` (cloned to `~/lab/challenge-c1`, local state)
goal: Write a parameterised `audit` definition that flags any resource whose `env` tag is not in the array parameter `allowedEnvs`, assign it at the scope of `rg-{user}-c1` only with `allowedEnvs = ["dev", "test"]`, and see the seeded group (tagged `env = "sandbox"`) reported non-compliant.
constraints: Assign at the resource group's scope, never the subscription: the lab's own assignments must not change. The effect is the literal `audit`, so nothing is refused.
verify_text: Dojo Cloud Policy (the student's own subscription, read-only): an assignment whose scope is `rg-{user}-c1`, in enforcement mode `Default`, whose definition has the literal effect `audit`, declares the parameter `allowedEnvs` and whose rule mentions `tags['env']`, lists `rg-{user}-c1` as non-compliant; and `main.tf` on `main` of `{user}/challenge-c1` declares an `azurerm_resource_group_policy_assignment` (push it). Not checked: the exact parameter value.
isolation: the assignment's scope is the student's own resource group `rg-{user}-c1` in their private subscription, so it can only ever judge that group; the cloud check reads only the checking student's own Policy blade (no account argument), and the repo is their own.
hints: Lab 5's allowed-images rule already compares a field with an array parameter.
`notIn` with "[parameters('allowedEnvs')]", and the assignment's `parameters = jsonencode({ allowedEnvs = { value = [...] } })`.
seed: `dojo-challenge start c1` creates `{user}/challenge-c1` (owned by the student, cloned to `~/lab/challenge-c1`): a `main.tf` with the resource group `rg-{user}-c1` tagged `env = "sandbox"` and two TODOs, a starter `rules/allowed-envs.json` full of `TODO`s, provider files with local state, and a README with the brief.
answer: `dojo-challenge start c1`, `cd ~/lab/challenge-c1`. Rule: `{"if": {"field": "tags['env']", "notIn": "[parameters('allowedEnvs')]"}, "then": {"effect": "audit"}}`. In `main.tf`: `resource "azurerm_policy_definition" "allowed_envs" { name = "allowed-envs-c1", policy_type = "Custom", mode = "All", display_name = "Allowed env tags (c1)", policy_rule = file("${path.module}/rules/allowed-envs.json"), parameters = jsonencode({ allowedEnvs = { type = "Array" } }) }` and `resource "azurerm_resource_group_policy_assignment" "allowed_envs" { name = "allowed-envs-c1", resource_group_id = azurerm_resource_group.c1.id, policy_definition_id = azurerm_policy_definition.allowed_envs.id, parameters = jsonencode({ allowedEnvs = { value = ["dev", "test"] } }) }`. `tofu init && tofu apply`, `git add . && git commit -m 'c1' && git push origin main`, `dojo-check c1`, then `tofu destroy`.
